components.name: Toggle tile — on (representative native equivalent)
components.description: Representative rendered equivalent of ToggleTile, not shipping SwiftUI source. CSS AccentColor approximates the native accent; shipping Theme.controlFill additionally constrains sRGB luminance to 0.18 for white-text contrast, which this static specimen does not reproduce. CanvasText and inline SVG stand in for native text and SF Symbols. Browser pixels approximate native points; focus behavior is illustrative. The on/off transition is not simulated.

components.name: Toggle tile — off (representative native equivalent)
components.description: Representative rendered equivalent of inactive ToggleTile. Neutral fills are extracted; browser semantic text, font metrics, focus, and SVG are platform approximations, not new source tokens. Not shipping HTML.

components.name: Action tile (representative native equivalent)
components.description: Representative rendered equivalent of a Home action tile. Browser shadow, SF Symbol substitute, semantic text, and focus are approximations; the specimen has no network action and is not shipping source.

components.name: Tab navigation (representative native equivalent)
components.description: Representative rendered equivalent of the five panel tabs; selected state is static. Inline SVGs approximate SF Symbols. Browser semantic colors, focus, and caption metrics do not define shipping tokens. Native source additionally supplies Command–1 through Command–5.

components.name: Node search field (representative native equivalent)
components.description: Representative rendered equivalent of the native rounded-border TextField shown for groups with more than ten members. This deliberately uses a browser-native field: its border, radius, focus, and metrics are not extracted custom SwiftUI tokens. No custom error or focus system is implied.

narrative.overview:
TinyClash uses the confirmed Stash for Mac reference through native macOS controls, a softly tinted canvas, raised rounded panels, and a system accent that identifies selection and enabled proxy controls. This is an operational interface: readable state and familiar behavior take precedence over decoration. Its shipping surface is a native SwiftUI menu-bar panel, not a web application or a reduced desktop window.

The system follows macOS light and dark appearance. Standard system text and SF Symbols carry the interface; rounded, monospaced digits distinguish live network values. Simplified Chinese labels stay compact, with secondary text used for profile names, node details, and supporting information.

This document records the implementation in `Sources/TinyClash/Views/Theme.swift`, `Components.swift`, `Panel/MenuPanel.swift`, `Panel/HomeTab.swift`, and `Panel/ProxiesTab.swift`. Values are source-extracted, not a claim of rendered validation. `PRODUCT.md` and the existing menu-panel surface brief supply the confirmed direction, not additional tokens. The frontmatter uses native points and records literal source colors as CSS sRGB percentages without rounding. Native semantic colors and semantic font sizes remain system-resolved; no fixed substitutes are prescribed. The sidecar's HTML/CSS specimens are representative rendered equivalents only, not shipping source.
keyCharacteristics: Adaptive cool-neutral canvas and raised panels.
System accent for selection and enabled controls; semantic color for network state.
Native system typography, SF Symbols, and rounded tabular numerals.
Compact spacing, continuous rounded corners, and restrained interaction feedback.

rules.name: The Semantic Latency Rule
rules.body: Preserve the implemented thresholds: nil is untested, zero is timeout, positive values below 500 ms are green, 500–999 ms are orange, and 1000 ms or more are red. Pair color with a readable value, “超时”, or an explicit placeholder; the decorative health strip is not the sole reading.

rules.name: The Stable Numerals Rule
rules.body: Use `Theme.numeral` for live speed, traffic, and latency readouts so rounded forms and monospaced digits remain consistent; keep surrounding labels in the default system design.

rules.name: The Raised Panel Rule
rules.body: Reuse the existing tonal surface and restrained shadow for raised cards; do not add decorative outlines to `PanelBackground`. Retain native dividers and field borders where the component already uses them.

dos: **Do** follow macOS appearance, native controls, SF Symbols, and system text hierarchy.
**Do** reuse the established panel, tile, chip, and spacing values rather than introducing parallel scales.
**Do** preserve visible text and state indicators alongside semantic network colors.
**Do** distinguish untested latency, timeout, a stopped core, and a running core without traffic takeover.
**Do** keep browser specimens explicitly labeled as representative native-component equivalents, not SwiftUI implementation code.
donts: **Don't** replace adaptive system accent or semantic network colors with an invented fixed brand palette.
**Don't** turn the menu-bar interface into a main-window layout or add unsupported responsive breakpoints.
**Don't** add decorative borders to the existing raised-card treatment or remove native dividers on that pretext.
**Don't** bypass the existing Reduce Motion checks on toggle, press, or hover feedback.
**Don't** treat synthesized tonal ramps, browser focus styling, or browser component metrics as extracted shipping tokens.
